findings.title: Object of import() promises starts loading every app eagerly
findings.body: Each `import(...)` in the object literal is evaluated as soon as this module is loaded, so all ~30 app modules are fetched and evaluated on first import of `@calcom/app-store`, whether or not they are used. The PR title says 'async import', but this does not make loading lazy; it only changes the access pattern. A consumer that needs one app pays for all of them. Lazy loading would need a function per entry, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, with call sites updated to match.

findings.title: Rejected import promises are unhandled and any uncaught access breaks silently
findings.body: Because every entry is a promise created at module load, a failing import (missing dependency, syntax error in one app) produces an unhandled promise rejection when nobody has awaited that entry. Callers that index the store without `await` (any call site not updated in this PR) now receive a Promise, so `"lib" in app` is false and the code silently treats the app as not implemented, e.g. `getCalendar` logs a 'not implemented' warning and returns null.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now yields promises in the `calendar` field while staying synchronous
findings.body: `getCalendarCredentials` is still a synchronous function, so `getCalendar(credential)` returns a Promise that is stored as the `calendar` field. Any other caller of this exported function that uses `.calendar` as a Calendar object (not awaiting it) will break. Only `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to `await item.calendar`. Other consumers of this exported API are not updated in the diff and should be checked, or the function should become async.

findings.title: Async forEach drops calendar deletions for recurring cancellations
findings.body: The `.forEach(async (credential) => {...})` callback pushes into `apiDeletes` only after `await getCalendar(...)` and the inner loop. Nothing awaits the callback promises, and `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs with the array as it was before the callbacks finished. As a result the calendar deletions are fire-and-forget: the handler reports success before they complete, and any rejection (e.g. from `deleteEvent`) becomes an unhandled rejection rather than an error surfaced to the caller. Use `for...of` with `await` or `Promise.all` over mapped promises, as the non-recurring branch already does.

findings.title: Async forEach makes the try/catch around calendar/video deletion ineffective
findings.body: The `try { bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) } catch` block cannot catch errors from the async callbacks, since forEach does not return or await them. Previously `getCalendar` was synchronous and the try covered failures; now any error from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` / `deleteMeeting` is an unhandled promise rejection and the reschedule flow continues without logging it. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try.

findings.title: Same async forEach issue: calendar/video deletions are not awaited and errors are unhandled
findings.body: The `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` callbacks are not awaited, so the deletion of the previous calendar event and video meeting runs in the background. The surrounding try/catch no longer catches anything. Rejections surface as unhandled promise rejections, and the caller cannot know whether the deletions succeeded.

findings.title: Reschedule mutation fires calendar/video deletions without awaiting them
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` is not awaited, so the mutation returns before the old calendar event and video meeting are deleted. Failures become unhandled rejections. Rescheduling can therefore report success while the previous event stays on the calendar, or while errors go unreported. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))`.

findings.title: Unrelated blank-line change in getCalendarCredentials
findings.body: A blank line is added before `return credentials.length ? ...` with no functional change. It adds noise to an already large async conversion.
